replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed items:

- Automated abuse of a public entry point: design says "Incoming emails come from anyone on the internet" — present, already covered by listed threat 3 (bulk mail driving LLM/send quota).
- Staff/admin screens rendering other people's content: the design states summaries go to "the sales team" but names no screen, portal or rendering surface — nothing in the text to attack, so not reported.
- Actions with no record of who did them: present ("forward emails and draft replies on behalf of the sales team") — covered by listed threat 5.
- Cacheable personal/financial documents or pages: nothing in the design mentions documents, downloads or pages — not present.
- Attacker-controlled text flowing into another interpreting system: present — attacker email text reaches outbound mail the agent sends ("can forward emails and draft replies on behalf of the sales team"); used as a mail relay to third parties this is **not covered** (listed threats cover exfiltration to the attacker and send-quota exhaustion, not attacker content delivered to victims under the company's identity).
- Of the unconfirmed threats, sender-identity trust ("Incoming emails come from anyone on the internet" plus replies on behalf of the team) is real and only partly touched by listed threat 4, which covers asking about other threads rather than impersonating a known party.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-04",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["email triage agent", "shared sales inbox", "summarisation step", "forward tool", "reply draft/send tool"],
    "dataStores": ["shared sales inbox"],
    "externalServices": ["inbound/outbound email"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["internet senders -> shared inbox", "agent -> outbound mail as sales team"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": true
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Agent used as a trusted mail relay to send attacker content to third parties",
      "scenario": "Anyone emails the sales inbox with content and an instruction to forward or reply to a chosen outside address. The agent can forward and send mail on behalf of the sales team, so the attacker's text (phishing link, fake invoice, changed bank details) reaches victims carrying the company's sales identity. Victims trust it because it genuinely comes from the sales team, so the harm lands on third parties and the company's mail reputation rather than on the inbox owner.",
      "component": "forward / reply tool on behalf of sales team",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "integrity" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "An agent reads the shared sales inbox, summarises each email and can forward emails and draft replies on behalf of the sales team." },
        { "quote": "Incoming emails come from anyone on the internet." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V5.3.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-441"],
      "plainLanguage": "A stranger can make the agent mail his own text to other people as if the sales team wrote it, so his scam arrives with your company's name on it.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Restrict and review agent-sent mail to third parties",
        "given": "an incoming email asks the agent to forward or reply to an address not already part of the existing thread",
        "when": "the agent attempts to send that mail on behalf of the sales team",
        "then": "the send is blocked pending explicit human approval, recipients are limited to the original thread participants or an approved list, and outbound volume per inbound message is capped"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Spoofed customer address gets the agent to reply with that account's information",
      "scenario": "The inbox accepts mail from anyone and the agent replies on behalf of the sales team with no sender verification described. An attacker forges the From address of a known customer or an internal manager and asks for their quote, contract copy or account status. The agent treats the claimed identity as real and sends the reply to the attacker-controlled return path, handing over another party's commercial and personal details without ever compromising an account.",
      "component": "inbound email handling / reply generation",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "one", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Incoming emails come from anyone on the internet." },
        { "quote": "summarises each email and can forward emails and draft replies on behalf of the sales team" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-290"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone can fake a customer's email address and the agent will reply to the faker with that customer's quote or contract details.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Verify sender identity before the agent discloses account information",
        "given": "an inbound email requests information tied to a specific customer or account",
        "when": "the agent prepares a reply containing that information",
        "then": "the sender must pass authentication checks (SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment and a known-contact match) and otherwise the reply is withheld for human handling"
      }
    }
  ]
}
